questions.stem: What is a token in a large language model?

options.A: A unit of text the model counts, bills, and generates
options.B: A password stored beside every approved user account
options.C: A permanent memory record kept after each finished chat
options.D: A certificate that proves the model completed training

questions.rationale: A token is the text unit the model reads and writes. Providers bill by tokens and context limits count tokens.

questions.stem: A hallucination is a confident answer that is not supported by facts or evidence.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.rationale: Hallucination means the model produces fluent text that is untrue or unsupported.

questions.stem: What does the context window limit for one model call?

options.A: How many GPUs the provider keeps online overnight for training
options.B: How many documents exist in the whole vector index store
options.C: How many users may register for the product each year
options.D: How many tokens of input and output fit in that call

questions.rationale: The context window caps how much text, measured in tokens, can be present in one call.

questions.stem: How does a generative AI solution differ from the model alone?

options.A: The model alone already stores every company policy forever
options.B: The solution adds application layers around the model
options.C: The solution removes the need for any prompts or tool calls
options.D: The model alone measures cost, privacy, and user permissions

questions.rationale: A solution wraps the model with retrieval, tools, policies, and product behaviour. The raw model is only one part.

questions.stem: Why request structured output such as JSON from a model call?

options.A: So the model can skip the system role on every request made
options.B: So embeddings are no longer needed for any retrieval step later
options.C: So the application can validate fields before using results
options.D: So the context window grows automatically without any hard limit

questions.rationale: Structured output gives a predictable shape the application can check and parse. It does not remove roles, retrieval, or context limits.

questions.stem: What does retrieval-augmented generation provide at answer time?

options.A: Selected evidence from external knowledge sources
options.B: Permanent retraining on every private company file
options.C: Unrestricted write access to every connected database
options.D: A guarantee that every generated claim is always correct

questions.rationale: RAG retrieves relevant passages and adds them to the prompt for the current answer. It does not retrain the model or guarantee correctness.

questions.stem: RAG updates the model weights each time a new document is indexed.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.rationale: RAG retrieves evidence at request time. Indexing documents does not retrain model weights.

questions.stem: What is an embedding in a retrieval system?

options.A: A readable summary stored beside each source passage
options.B: A permissions label that grants admin rights to users
options.C: A generated answer returned for the latest user question
options.D: A numerical vector that represents an item's meaning

questions.rationale: An embedding is a numerical vector used to compare meaning between queries and chunks.

questions.stem: What does hybrid search combine in a retrieval pipeline?

options.A: Model fine-tuning and unlimited context windows for every call
options.B: Keyword matching and vector similarity scoring together
options.C: Password hashing and automatic GPU scaling rules overnight
options.D: Streaming display and monthly invoice generation for billing

questions.rationale: Hybrid search uses both keyword and vector signals so exact terms and meaning both help retrieval.

questions.stem: Why evaluate retrieval quality separately from answer generation?

options.A: Because embeddings delete the original text after indexing finishes
options.B: Because keyword search cannot run in the same system as vectors
options.C: Because a wrong answer may come from weak retrieval or generation
options.D: Because generation quality never depends on the retrieved passages

questions.rationale: Separate checks show whether the index returned useful evidence or the model mishandled good evidence.

questions.stem: Who runs a tool after the model returns a tool call?

options.A: The language model runs it during its own inference process
options.B: Your application code runs it, or can refuse to run it
options.C: The vector database runs it before any answer is written
options.D: The embedding service runs it whenever text is retrieved

questions.rationale: The model only requests a tool. Application code decides whether to execute that request.

questions.stem: An agent should look up tools in an allow-list instead of running any name the model returns.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.rationale: Dictionary lookup on an allow-list keeps execution limited to approved functions.

questions.stem: Why is a vague tool description such as "Gets leave data" a problem?

options.A: The model lacks clear timing, scope, and call exclusions
options.B: JSON Schema rejects descriptions shorter than one full page
options.C: Vector stores cannot store tool text written in plain English
options.D: Models can only call tools when their description field is empty

questions.rationale: The description tells the model when to call the tool. Vague text leads to guessing and over-calling.

questions.stem: Why does every agent need a step cap?

options.A: GPUs reject more than one tool request by hardware design
options.B: Free tiers always block long loops before any cost appears
options.C: A failed goal can repeat paid calls while history grows
options.D: Models forget earlier tool results after exactly five steps

questions.rationale: Without a cap, an unsatisfiable goal can keep requesting tools while cost and history grow.

questions.stem: How does agentic RAG differ from plain RAG?

options.A: Plain RAG never retrieves; agentic RAG retrieves only one passage
options.B: Agentic RAG deletes the retriever and trains a model each turn
options.C: Agentic RAG removes citations so the final answer can stay short
options.D: Plain RAG retrieves once; agentic RAG decides whether to search

questions.rationale: In agentic RAG, retrieval is a tool the model may choose to call, refine, or skip.

questions.stem: Caching is the cost method that can reduce both cost and delay.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.rationale: Day 4 lists caching first because it can cut both spend and latency.

questions.stem: Why is indirect prompt injection often more serious than direct injection?

options.A: Direct injection cannot appear inside any authenticated user session log
options.B: The attacker may never use the system, and poisoned text can persist
options.C: Indirect injection only works when streaming output has been disabled
options.D: Direct injection always bypasses every log and audit trail in the product

questions.rationale: Indirect injection can be planted by someone who never logs in, and one poisoned passage can affect many later questions.

questions.stem: A sentence telling the model to ignore instructions in retrieved text is enough on its own as a security control.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.rationale: A defensive instruction is only a preference in the same channel the attacker uses. It must not be the sole control.

questions.stem: Where should irreversible tool permissions be enforced?

options.A: In application policy outside the model before tools run
options.B: Only inside a longer system prompt with stronger wording
options.C: Only in the vector index metadata for each document chunk
options.D: Only by raising temperature so risky actions become rare

questions.rationale: The model can be influenced by injection. Fixed policy, sandboxing, and least privilege must sit in application code.

questions.stem: What does governance require a team to be able to state after an incident?

options.A: Only the brand name of the largest model that was available that day
options.B: Only the number of embeddings stored in the vector database index
options.C: Who authorised the system, what it could do, and what it did
options.D: Only the marketing slogan used on the product landing page copy

questions.rationale: Governance means you can account for authorisation, permitted actions, and actual behaviour after something goes wrong.
